about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Friday's short session has corn trading the holiday outside markets; heavy crop-insurance claims after this year's weather extremes underline uneven yields but do not change the large US supply. Dec sits just above 438 support.
events: Weather extremes trigger crop-insurance claims across the Corn Belt (Brownfield)
Corn traders return from Thanksgiving break (Barchart)
USDA survey participation falls over 34%, raising data doubts (AgroLatam)

soybeans.fundamental: Jan beans broke above 1,269.5 resistance on biofuel-driven crush demand and the stronger real, which makes Brazilian beans dearer in dollars. Against that, rains in Mato Grosso have eased El Niño damage fears for Brazil's new crop, which caps the supply-scare part of the story.
events: Rains ease El Niño crop fears in Mato Grosso (Bloomberg)
Biofuels boom adds support to soybean prices (Brownfield)

meal.fundamental: Meal rides the bean rally, but record crush to meet biofuel oil demand keeps meal supply heavy, so gains are leaning on the complex rather than on meal's own balance.
events: Soybeans rally in the short Friday session (Barchart)
Biofuel demand keeps crush running hard (Brownfield)
Brazil rains ease crop worries (Bloomberg)

oil.fundamental: Biofuel demand is the support story for soyoil, while stalled Indonesian palm tenders on weak demand show the veg-oil complex is not tight; crude's intraday drop is a headwind for biodiesel margins.
events: Biofuels boom supports soy complex (Brownfield)
Indonesia palm oil tenders stall on weak demand (Bloomberg)
WTI ~82.8 (-1.9%) (OilPrice)

events: Wheat heads into a shortened Friday session (Barchart)

palm.fundamental: Stalled Indonesian tenders point to soft export demand even with tight local supply, and crude's intraday reversal removes part of the biodiesel support; India's shift back toward palm remains the main offset.

WTI ~82.8 (-1.9%) (OilPrice)

natgas.fundamental: No US supply shock; abroad, Australia's 20% domestic reservation law and Russia-China pricing friction are longer-term LNG-market stories rather than near-term US demand drivers.
events: Australia passes 20% gas reservation law (Reuters, Bloomberg)
Russian domestic gas price may complicate China talks (Reuters)
Iran and Turkey extend gas deal (Bloomberg)

crude.fundamental: Crude reversed lower intraday as Iraq lifted exports to about 3.6m b/d, offsetting the earlier loading-delay headlines; OPEC+ is expected to roll over Q1 targets, and the report of US pressure on Iraq and Venezuela to leave OPEC raises questions about future quota discipline. Stockpiling demand into 2027 is cited as a floor.
events: Iraq boosts oil exports to ~3.6m b/d (OilPrice)
US pushed Iraq and Venezuela to consider leaving OPEC (Reuters)
OPEC+ likely to roll over Q1 targets (Reuters, Bloomberg)

ulsd.fundamental: Distillates stay the firm part of the barrel: Russia extended its jet-fuel export ban to March after refinery attacks, and the global diesel balance is seen moving into deficit by Q2 2027. Refinery outages at Jazan and Amuay add to that.
events: Russia extends jet fuel export ban to March (Bloomberg)
Global diesel market seen in deficit in Q2 2027 (Reuters)
Attack halts part of Aramco's Jazan refinery (Reuters)

rbob.fundamental: Gasoline remains the weak link of the barrel in the seasonal demand trough; crude-led strength is lifting it in sympathy rather than any change in gasoline balances.
events: Gasoline falling while diesel stays expensive (OilPrice)
WTI ~85.1 (+1.7%) on Middle East supply risk (Reuters, WSJ)
